Prepared statements (also known as parameterized queries) are useful for SQL injection defense because they strictly separate SQL code from data. When a prepared statement is used, the database first compiles the SQL query structure with placeholders for parameters. The actual data values are then sent separately to the database engine, which treats them strictly as data rather than executable code.
